claude.reason: The six-session base is visibly tight and orderly in the shaded region near $47–$50, with no wide overlapping bars or internal breakdowns, and the signal bar closed near its high on more than double the prior session's volume. The notes also flag that prior breakouts worked 0 of 4 in the last 60 sessions, which is a meaningful caution even though it carries no grade vote.
claude.key_risk: The prior leg's ER of 0.39 falls just below the A+ linearity threshold and the move has already more than doubled from its start, making follow-through less reliable than a fresher setup.
claude.entry_note: Skip if the open gaps above the base high of $50.54 or if the first 30 minutes show a fade back below the prior close of $48.62.

_contract.schema_version: 2. The page refuses any other number rather than guessing at an older shape.
_contract.generated: When this file was written, ISO-8601 UTC. The page reads staleness off run.session, run.calendar and the browser's clock in ET; missing calendar evidence stays unknown.
_contract.app: Who wrote the file: the app name, its version, and rules_version -- a 12-hex digest of the rules block, so two nights under different constants never read as one screener.
_contract.cover: The night's verdict as sentences: h1, dek, the primary action's label and anchor, and the verb. Composed from the numbers below; never edited by hand.
_contract.run: The run that produced this file: session, session_state, expected_session, status (ok|degraded|closed|failed), problems (stage, kind, message -- kind is one of seven words and the page prints one fixed sentence per kind), versioned coverage ledger, universe snapshot provenance, input_basis (Alpaca daily feed, split adjustment and sessions), counts, email state, timings. run.sanitised counts the non-finite numbers replaced with null on the way in. run.timing is a different fact from the two above it: the session tonight's plans are FOR and the instants its entry window is scheduled between, offset and all. run.calendar records XNYS/library/version, measured/previous/next dates, actual open/close/shortened hours, completion buffer and a bounded browser schedule. Schedules may change. A record without it is one published before the field existed, and the page says entry timing is unavailable rather than guessing at a deadline. run.input_tolerance says whether a degraded acceptance is only the stale tail the recorded tolerance allows -- status ok beside acceptance degraded means exactly that -- and names those stocks; run.stale_followup reads the previous publication's stale stocks again from this run's fetch and never turns a late bar into a signal. run.reader_usage is what the night's chart reads cost in the API's own units -- calls sent, replies received, the four token classes -- under the model the run asked; it carries no price. run.intraday is the minute bars read for plans whose first day the daily bar could not place (a day that reached the trigger after the open): what tonight needed, asked for, fetched and stored under docs/intraday/, and the failures by kind; a plan walked from them names its object in minute_evidence. run.earnings is each published ticket's earnings warning, estimated from the company's SEC results filings (8-K item 2.02) a year back and read against the plan's hold window: an estimate and never an announced date, a warning and never a refusal, and a ticket SEC did not answer for says unknown.
_contract.nights: The last twenty runs as a ring: session, status, published_at. The reliability dots.
_contract.account: The configured sizing assumptions every plan below was computed from: equity, risk per trade, the position cap, the slot count. Not a balance, not settled cash, not buying power.
_contract.rules: Every strategy constant, keyed by module. Archived so the record says which screener made it.
_contract.breadth: The Market Monitor for the session and the regime verdict with its reasons verbatim. The size multiplier is the regime's; the plans already carry it.
_contract.bursts: Every 4% or $ breakout the scan found, graded, with its plan when it has one, its summary sentence and its series (last 120 bars, trades and the closest miss only). Scored or refused, a burst is here; a name that never burst is not. volume_vs_prior is the session's volume over the previous session's for every row, the $-only ones included (null when the previous session printed none); quality.burst holds the checklist's copy at two places.
_contract.trades: Tickers of the bursts to trade next session, ranked; those with order lines first. On a red regime this is empty whatever the grades say.
_contract.beyond_cap: Tickers of A-quality bursts with a plan and no ticket: withheld by the stop rule at the limit, past the slots or the configured equity, or sized to no whole share. Each has a reason in cash_budget.cut. Not checklist refusals.
_contract.cash_budget: Combined reaction and anticipation model allocation, reaction rank first: new tickets, principal reserved for unfinished model plans, model slots used, and every cut ticket with its setup kind and reason. Partial model sales do not free capacity. Never a balance, settled cash or buying power.
_contract.watchlist: Anticipation names: top (with a plan each) and also_quiet, with counts. Alerts, not trades.
_contract.open_plans: Every published plan still inside its window, replayed to this session as a model: status word, the instruction sentence, and for an uncertain fill the reason. SpicyStock does not know what you hold: a plan you never took is a row to ignore.
_contract.scorecard: All retained published plans in the stated window, including pending and missing evidence. Disjoint outcome counts reconcile to plans; rates use resolved plans alone, with an explicit denominator and minimum sample. Public model results, independent of personal selections.
_contract.closest_miss: On any night, the highest-scored burst not in trades and why it missed; the page shows it when trades is empty. Null when every burst is a trade or there were none.
_contract.funnel: Where every discovered reaction candidate and every listed anticipation setup stopped: one terminal stage each, in the order the run applies its gates, so the stage counts sum to the discovered count. Derived from the fields above and re-derived by the validator; the labels the page and the mail print travel with it. A stage is the record's own accounting of its gates, never a judgement of the setup and never an entry.
_contract.observations: Public coverage of every published saveable signal, independent of local saves. Each signal keeps its own identity and 21-calendar-day window. Symbols carry the latest real bar plus up to 20 dated observations from already-fetched frames; missing bars stay missing, and missing frames retain earlier actual observations. This is research coverage, never a quote feed or personal trading history.
